about: The front door: places and curiosities pinned on Ortelius's map of Tartary (M047). xy is in full-resolution pixels of the Library of Congress image. Only readings marked sure in the search notes are kept. The Latin is as read from the sheet and may be partial.

pins.on_map: Volga, et Edel, ol: Rha fl.
Mar de Bachu, olim Mare Caspium, et Hyrcanum.
Cambalu Cataie metropolis, habet 28. mill: in circuitu.

sights.title: The Duke of Muscovy's tent
sights.what: A large tent with an armed ruler at its door, beside the words 'borders of the Duke of Muscovy'.
sights.latin: DVCIS MOSCOVIAE CONFINIA.

sights.title: The Great Khan's camp
sights.what: Tents with the ruler seated at the door. The caption says Great Khan means emperor in the Tartar tongue, and calls him the greatest prince of Asia.
sights.latin: Magnus Cham, (quod lingua Tartarorum Imperatorem sonat) maximus Asie princeps.

sights.title: What the map claims to show
sights.what: The map's own summary, held up by two figures: all Tartary and the rest of eastern Asia that obeys the Great Khan, bounded by the Ob, the Volga, the Caspian, Tibet, the Caromoran river and the ocean.
sights.latin: Continet hec tabula oem Tartariam, cum reliqua Asie Orientalioris usq3 Oceanu Eoum parte, Magno Chamo obediente: Cuius imperium Obij fl: Kataia lacu; Volga fl: Mari Caspio, Chesel flu: Ussonte monte, Thebet regione, Caromoram fluuio, & Oceano terminatur.

sights.title: The ten lost tribes
sights.what: The land of Arsareth. The note says the ten tribes of Israel withdrew here and took the place of the Scythians as Totars or Tartars, and ties the name Cathay to them.
sights.latin: ARSARETH. Hic 10 Tribus secessere, et Totatoru sive Tartarorum loco Scythice substituerunt. Vnde Gauthe seu Gauthay a summa Dei gloria asserenda ibi dicti sunt, et hinc Cathay clariss: Regnum.

sights.title: A horde named for a tribe of Israel
sights.what: A horde in the far north is lettered as the Nephthalites, and the note says they are named after Naphtali, one of the ten tribes of Israel.
sights.latin: Nepthalitarum horda, Nepthalite a 10 Tribuum Israelis nomine Neptali dicti sunt

sights.title: The king of Tabor
sights.what: A note on Tabor or Tybur, which it calls the navel of the Tartars' country. It says their king came to France in 1540, to King Francis I, and was later burned at Mantua under Charles V.
sights.latin: Tabor seu Tybur, umbilicarius Tatarorum regio, ubi licet olim libros sacros perdidissent, sunt tamen uniti sub uno rege, qui 1540 in Galliam usq3 ad regem Franciscum illius nominis primum venit, et postea a Carolo V. Mantue igne sue infidelitatis poenas luit

sights.title: Prester John's kingdom
sights.what: A note on Argon: once, it says, the Christian kingdom of Prester John in Asia, founded by Saint Thomas.
sights.latin: ARGON. Christianorum olim regnu noie Presbiteri Iois in Asia erat, a D. Thoma ibi institutum, ut Romane corresponderet ecclesie

sights.title: Printing, a thousand years early
sights.what: A note beside Tangut: people here, it is said, had the art of printing a thousand years ago.
sights.latin: Hic arte imprimendi ante mille, ut ferunt, annos habuerunt.

sights.title: The Strait of Anian
sights.what: The Strait of Anian, the imagined sea passage separating Asia from America.
sights.latin: STRETTO DI ANIAN

sights.title: Japan, attacked in vain
sights.what: A note below Japan: this is the island Marco Polo called Zipangri, which the Great Khan once attacked in war, in vain.
sights.latin: Iapan insula, a M. Paulo Veneto Zipangri dicta, olim Chryse, a Magno Cham olim bello petita sed frustra.

sights.title: America, across the strait
sights.what: The west coast of North America, lettered 'part of America or the New World', with Sierra Nevada and California further south.
sights.latin: AMERICAE VEL NOVI ORBIS PARS

sights.title: The map’s title
sights.what: Map of Tartary, or of the kingdom of the Great Khan.
sights.latin: Tartariae sive Magni Chami Regni typus.

sights.title: The Scythian Ocean
sights.what: The Scythian Ocean is fresh water, according to Pliny, who says there are many islands in it, as does Marco Polo of Venice; but neither gives their location or number. This is the map’s report of those authors.
sights.latin: Oceanus Scythicus dulcis est Plinio auctore, qui multas in eo insulas esse dicit, ut etiam M. Paul: Venetus: sed neuter neque situm neque numerum tradit.

sights.title: Tartary, Sarmatia, and Scythia
sights.what: Tartary, which comprises Asian Sarmatia and both Scythias of the ancients. “Both Scythias” refers to the ancient geographical division on either side of Mount Imaus.
sights.latin: Tartaria, quae Sarmatiam Asiaticam, et utramque Scythiam veterum comprehendit.

sights.title: Turkestan and the ten tribes
sights.what: The region of Turkestan, from which the allies of the ten tribes on this side of the mountains were summoned by the Persians 900 years ago against the arms of Muhammad the Ishmaelite. The wording and chronology are the map’s own.
sights.latin: Turchestan Regio unde cismontani 10. Tribuum socij ante 900 annos sunt accersiti a Persis contra Ismaelitae Mahumedis arma.

sights.title: Aromatic reeds
sights.what: Here aromatic reed grows abundantly. Calamus aromaticus is a fragrant reed or sweet flag.
sights.latin: Hic magnus proventus calami aromatici.

sights.title: Ruby deposits
sights.what: Here ruby gemstones are found.
sights.latin: Hic Rubini gemmae reperiuntur.

sights.title: The burial mountain of the emperors
sights.what: Mount Altai, where all the emperors of Tartary are buried, appears to be described by Hayton the Armenian under the name Belgian.
sights.latin: Mons Althay, ubi omnes Tartariae imperatores sepeliuntur, ab Haytone Armeno sub nomine Belgian describi videtur.

sights.title: The Danes or Danites
sights.what: The horde of the Danes or Danites; the accompanying gloss reads “casting down, descent, or expulsion.” The map associates the Danes with the biblical Danites.
sights.latin: Danorum sive Danitarum horda 1. deiectio sive descensio aut expulsio.

sights.title: Marco Polo’s falcon island
sights.what: Island of falcons, according to Marco Polo of Venice.
sights.latin: Insula falconum, M. Pauli Veneti.

sights.title: Cambalu’s circumference
sights.what: Cambalu, the chief city of Cathay, measures 28 miles around its circumference. The map’s historical distance is retained without conversion to modern miles.
sights.latin: Cambalu Cataiae metropolis, habet 28. mill: in circuitu.

sights.title: Stones burned instead of wood
sights.what: From these mountains stones are dug out which people use for the fire instead of wood. The note describes coal.
sights.latin: His montibus eruuntur lapides, quibus utuntur ad focum loco lignorum.

sights.title: Quinsai, the city of heaven
sights.what: Quinsai, that is, the city of heaven.
sights.latin: Quinsai id est civitas celi.

sights.title: Rhubarb in the mountains
sights.what: Rhubarb grows in these mountains.
sights.latin: His montibus Rhabarbarum provenit.

sights.title: A marble bridge
sights.what: A marble bridge, 300 paces long. The abbreviation pass. denotes paces; the map does not give a modern unit conversion.
sights.latin: Pons marmoreus 300. pass:

sights.title: Meaco, Japan’s chief city
sights.what: Meaco, the chief city of the island. Meaco is the historical name used here for Kyoto.
sights.latin: Meaco insulae civitas primaria.

sights.title: Samarkand, seat of Tamerlane
sights.what: Samarkand, formerly the seat of the great Tamerlane.
sights.latin: Samarchand. magni Tamber: quondam sedes.

sights.title: Bargu’s marshland
sights.what: Bargu, a marshy region.
sights.latin: Bargu regio palustris.

sights.title: Cape Tabin in Pliny
sights.what: Cape Tabin, according to Pliny. Prom. abbreviates promontory or cape; Plin. identifies Pliny as the authority.
sights.latin: Tabin Prom: Plin.

sights.title: The printing privilege
sights.what: With privilege. This indicates an official privilege protecting the publication.
sights.latin: Cum Privilegio.

translation_audit.method: Read against the full-resolution Library of Congress sheet. New transcriptions expand scribal abbreviations and normalize u/v, ligatures and long s; English translations are rendered from the Latin. Place-name buttons remain separate from inscription translations.
